evidence_boundary: Entries are synthesis categories grounded in the cited research notes. Component mappings are selection priors, not empirical performance claims.

failure_modes.description: Work stops serving the explicit goal, question, acceptance criteria, or requested deliverable.
observable_signals: The output answers a nearby question.
The success condition changes without an explicit scope revision.
A patch addresses behavior other than the reported problem.
escalation_path: Restate the authoritative task and completion evidence.
Request an explicit scope revision if the original task is no longer viable.

failure_modes.description: Work crosses from analysis, review, planning, or a bounded target into unrequested editing or action.
observable_signals: A review-only task modifies files.
A plan is executed without separate authorization.
Targets or source boundaries expand without approval.
escalation_path: Stop mutations or external actions.
Report any effects already produced and obtain explicit authority for recovery or continuation.

failure_modes.description: A necessary goal, premise, input, target, precondition, or completion criterion is absent or ambiguous.
observable_signals: Several materially different interpretations remain.
A required premise or target is silently guessed.
A tool, source, or project precondition is discovered only after failure.
escalation_path: Ask the smallest decision-relevant question.
If clarification is unavailable, return conditional or partial results and identify the missing input.

failure_modes.description: A factual or causal statement exceeds the available sources, observations, calculations, or authorized evidence boundary.
observable_signals: No source or observation supports a material statement.
The conclusion is stronger than the cited evidence.
Model memory is presented as inspected evidence.
escalation_path: Narrow or remove the unsupported statement.
Request or retrieve the missing evidence when authorized.

failure_modes.description: Exact numbers, dates, identifiers, rankings, probabilities, or thresholds are asserted without evidence at that granularity.
observable_signals: An approximate source becomes an exact value.
A numeric confidence is invented without a measurement method.
A decision changes on an unverified atomic fact.
escalation_path: Verify the decision-critical atom directly.
Otherwise reduce precision and state the evidence limit.

failure_modes.description: A citation is missing, misattributed, or does not directly support the adjacent claim.
observable_signals: The cited passage addresses a different proposition.
A citation supports only part of a compound claim.
Attribution is reconstructed after provenance was lost.
escalation_path: Re-open the original source and repair claim-level attribution.
Remove the citation or narrow the claim if entailment cannot be established.

failure_modes.description: Evidence is used outside its authority, date, version, population, jurisdiction, operating conditions, or intended purpose.
observable_signals: A secondary summary replaces an available controlling source.
Superseded material is presented as current.
A bounded result is generalized beyond tested conditions.
escalation_path: Re-evaluate authority and applicability for the exact context.
Qualify or abstain from claims that cannot be transferred safely.

failure_modes.description: Material sources, passages, files, dependencies, counterevidence, or review surfaces are omitted from the working set.
observable_signals: Known relevant material is absent.
Search uses only one narrow formulation.
A diff-only review misses a directly affected contract or test.
escalation_path: Expand retrieval along a stated relevance path.
Report uninspected or inaccessible material when the coverage budget is exhausted.

failure_modes.description: A derived claim, summary, state item, or action result cannot be traced to its source, tool call, file, passage, or version.
observable_signals: Notes lack stable source pointers.
A compressed summary becomes the only authority.
An action outcome has no request or audit identifier.
escalation_path: Recover the original source or observed state before relying on the derived item.
Mark dependent conclusions unverified if provenance cannot be restored.

failure_modes.description: Material disagreement is averaged away, omitted, or resolved without explicit authority and applicability rules.
observable_signals: Conflicting sources are reported as consensus.
The newest or majority source is selected automatically.
Different scopes are mistaken for factual conflict.
escalation_path: Preserve each supported position with authority and context.
Escalate a decision-critical unresolved conflict to the appropriate reviewer.

failure_modes.description: Material uncertainty is hidden, invented, over-quantified, or expressed without explaining its source and consequence.
observable_signals: A confident conclusion depends on missing evidence.
A probability is fabricated.
Generic hedging obscures which claim is uncertain.
escalation_path: Identify the uncertainty type and affected claim or action.
Narrow, qualify, seek evidence, or abstain according to consequence.

failure_modes.description: The first plausible diagnosis, plan, interpretation, design, or option is accepted before decision-relevant alternatives or checks are considered.
observable_signals: No rival explanation is considered despite ambiguity.
Editing begins before non-trivial localization or reproduction.
A consequential choice is made before criteria are fixed.
escalation_path: Generate only the minimum credible rival or discriminating check.
Return to clarification when alternatives reflect missing task information.

failure_modes.description: Evidence and tests are selected or interpreted only through the favored candidate, cause, or conclusion.
observable_signals: Only confirming observations are sought.
A review follows one defect class despite contrary signals.
Search terms assume the answer.
escalation_path: Seek one credible disconfirming observation or rival explanation.
Stop broadening when the candidate is directly established or the search budget ends.

failure_modes.description: Alternative generation, search, or delegation expands beyond the task's decision value, budget, or complexity ceiling.
observable_signals: Candidate count grows without new discrimination.
Parallel workers duplicate simple work.
A direct lookup becomes an open investigation.
escalation_path: Prune by failed constraint, inferior criterion, or budget rule.
Return the best bounded result and unresolved alternatives.

failure_modes.description: Facts, assumptions, state, or rejected conclusions leak between alternatives, counterfactuals, workers, or obsolete plans.
observable_signals: A counterfactual changes undeclared baseline facts.
A rejected branch re-enters the final answer as current.
One worker's assumptions are silently inherited by another.
escalation_path: Restore separate branch state and the authoritative baseline.
Recompute synthesis from explicitly accepted branch outputs.

failure_modes.description: Irrelevant, duplicated, or excessive context displaces task-critical facts and reduces usable attention.
observable_signals: Whole repositories or corpora are loaded without relevance filtering.
Tool logs crowd out requirements.
The same full references are loaded into every worker.
escalation_path: Reduce to a high-signal working set with retrieval pointers.
Split the task or return partial coverage if pressure remains.

failure_modes.description: A long-running or resumed workflow forgets completed work, decisions, failures, authority, or remaining tasks.
observable_signals: A resumed session repeats work.
Prior actions are guessed rather than observed.
A partial workflow has no completed/pending/unknown ledger.
escalation_path: Reconstruct state from authoritative project artifacts and observed external state.
Do not resume mutations until completed and unknown effects are separated.

failure_modes.description: A summary, plan, project profile, Skill reference, or cached observation no longer matches authoritative current state.
observable_signals: A progress map conflicts with current files or tests.
A source or policy version changed after the snapshot.
A Skill names obsolete paths or commands.
escalation_path: Refresh changed facts from their source of truth.
Invalidate dependent summaries and re-run only affected checks.

failure_modes.description: A required rule, literal, field, boundary, preference type, or acceptance criterion disappears from active reasoning or execution.
observable_signals: A required output field is omitted.
A hard constraint is treated as optional.
A protected literal is no longer tracked.
escalation_path: Restore a typed constraint ledger from authoritative inputs.
Re-evaluate dependent output or plan stages.

failure_modes.description: A transformation, repair, refactor, plan, or action breaks a protected behavior, interface, literal, relation, or safety condition.
observable_signals: A refactor changes observable behavior.
A rewrite alters a locked number or quotation.
A patch passes one test while breaking an adjacent contract.
escalation_path: Reject or revert the candidate output when authorized.
Narrow the change or escalate repair depth only with evidence.

failure_modes.description: A change expands into unrelated cleanup, redesign, or structural work beyond the localized requirement.
observable_signals: Unrelated files or behavior change.
A small defect causes a broad rewrite.
Diff size grows without causal necessity.
escalation_path: Reduce the patch to changes explained by the requirement or diagnosis.
Request explicit authority if evidence shows a structural repair is necessary.

failure_modes.description: A change is too shallow or narrow to satisfy the requirement, repair the cause, or update dependent contracts.
observable_signals: The symptom changes but the causal defect remains.
Callers, schemas, tests, or documentation remain inconsistent.
A local patch cannot satisfy the verified invariant.
escalation_path: Trace the minimum complete impact surface.
Escalate from local to structural repair only when a shallower boundary demonstrably fails.

failure_modes.description: Completion or correctness is asserted without checks proportionate to the claim, change, action, or consequence.
observable_signals: A call returning is treated as proof of the intended side effect.
A fix is claimed from syntax or one weak test.
A consequential claim receives only an ungrounded self-check.
escalation_path: Select a direct, deterministic, or independent check for the material failure mode.
Qualify completion if the required environment is unavailable.

failure_modes.description: Checks, judges, or repeated reviews cost more than the bounded task warrants or add no independent information.
observable_signals: Every validator is loaded for a low-impact direct task.
Several checks share the same evidence and assumptions.
Validation continues after acceptance criteria are met.
escalation_path: Retain only checks tied to material failure modes or independent evidence.
Stop when declared acceptance evidence is satisfied.

failure_modes.description: A test, metric, self-critique, benchmark, or proxy does not validly measure the actual requirement or context of use.
observable_signals: Tests conflict with the task specification.
A generator repeatedly endorses its own output.
A narrow benchmark is generalized to production capability.
escalation_path: Restate the property the validator must measure.
Replace or qualify invalid evidence and document untested conditions.

failure_modes.description: The wrong tool, malformed arguments, excessive reach, or an unsuitable execution pattern is used for the task requirement.
observable_signals: A tool is chosen because it is available rather than suitable.
Arguments do not match the tool contract.
A broad mutating tool is used where a scoped read would suffice.
escalation_path: Reclassify the required operation and inspect the tool contract.
Use a narrower tool or return the capability limitation.

failure_modes.description: The system claims access, memory, permissions, execution, or observed results that the host did not provide.
observable_signals: Browsing or test execution is described without a tool result.
A Skill claims persistence supplied only by prose.
Unknown capability is treated as available.
escalation_path: Remove the unsupported capability/result claim.
Request access, use an explicit fallback, or report the limitation.

failure_modes.description: A mutation is proposed or executed without explicit authority for the exact tool, target, scope, or effect.
observable_signals: Credential scope is treated as user consent.
Silence or tool availability is treated as approval.
A write occurs despite a review-only or denied state.
escalation_path: Stop before the side effect when authority is unknown or denied.
Provide a preview or approval packet and preserve any partial state.

failure_modes.description: A destructive, non-idempotent, external, or hard-to-reverse action lacks exact target resolution, retry safety, postconditions, or recovery handling.
observable_signals: A destructive target contains an unresolved variable or broad scope.
A timed-out mutation is repeated without reconciliation.
Rollback is assumed to erase all consequences.
escalation_path: Resolve exact targets and reconcile observed state before any retry.
Require explicit approval and a safe recovery path or stop before action.

failure_modes.description: Search, reasoning, revision, retries, or action loops continue without explicit success, failure, attempt, time, or cost bounds.
observable_signals: The agent continues after sufficient evidence.
Repeated attempts use the same failed strategy.
No completion or escalation threshold is stated.
escalation_path: Apply the declared budget and completion evidence.
Return accumulated evidence and the next safe step when the threshold is reached.

failure_modes.description: A continuation or delegation artifact omits authoritative state, completed work, validations, uncertainty, blockers, ownership, or the next action.
observable_signals: A new session must reconstruct prior work.
Verified facts and hypotheses are mixed.
A worker result has no scope or return contract.
escalation_path: Rebuild a bounded handoff packet from authoritative artifacts.
Do not transfer action authority implicitly.

failure_modes.description: Delegated work duplicates effort, leaves coverage gaps, loses shared state, or costs more to coordinate than the task itself.
observable_signals: Workers overlap while another subquestion is unassigned.
Tightly coupled steps are isolated without needed context.
Roles exist without distinct objectives or tool boundaries.
escalation_path: Collapse tightly coupled work into one context or repartition by bounded objective.
Reconcile coverage and conflicts before accepting synthesis.

failure_modes.description: A Skill, prompt, project instruction, tool, or agent package is too broad, loads at the wrong time, or claims capabilities outside its contract.
observable_signals: A Skill description matches an entire profession.
Conditional instructions load in every session.
One wrapper is created per component without a user-facing task procedure.
escalation_path: Return to the stable user job, activation boundary, and output contract.
Split or repackage only where a distinct capability boundary exists.

failure_modes.description: A Skill, lock, profile, dependency, source, or tool contract refers to an unpinned, incompatible, or superseded version.
observable_signals: A component silently resolves to latest.
A lock and installed snapshot disagree.
A cached source or API contract is obsolete.
escalation_path: Resolve the canonical version and show the mismatch.
Require review before changing pinned identities or dependent semantics.

failure_modes.description: The system either proceeds despite missing decision-critical evidence or authority, or refuses an entire task when a supported safe subset is possible.
observable_signals: A consequential unsupported claim is still asserted.
An unauthorized action proceeds.
One unresolved claim causes rejection of all bounded analysis.
escalation_path: Separate supported, qualified, conflicting, unavailable, and unassessed portions.
Block only the unsafe claim or action and provide the unblock condition.

failure_modes.description: Rules, evidence, terminology, or assumptions from one domain, source boundary, project, or task mode are applied to another without authority.
observable_signals: A domain rule is imported from an unrelated context.
Project-specific guidance leaks into a portable Skill.
Creative assumptions are presented as research evidence.
escalation_path: Restore the authorized domain, source, and project boundary.
Reclassify contaminated claims or state before continuing.
